t: A great eastern state of ancient China, founded on the Shandong peninsula by Jiang Ziya after the Zhou conquest.
Duke Huan and his minister Guan Zhong made Qi the first hegemon of the Zhou states in the 7th century BCE.
Its capital Linzi and the Jixia Academy made Qi a centre of wealth and philosophy until it surrendered to Qin in 221 BCE.
dyk: Qi's later ruling family, the Tian, descended from a prince of the State of Chen who had fled to Qi as a refugee in 672 BCE.
ev: Jiang Ziya receives Qi as a fief after the Zhou conquest
Duke Huan takes the throne and appoints Guan Zhong as minister
Duke Huan presides over the covenant of Kuiqiu as hegemon
The Zhou king recognises Tian He as ruler of Qi
Sun Bin's strategy defeats Wei at the Battle of Maling
Yue Yi's coalition army sacks Linzi
Tian Dan breaks the siege of Jimo and restores Qi
King Jian surrenders to Qin, completing the Qin unification
